title: cli-contract.md §2 omits principal from the canonical --json envelope it specifies
summary: src/output.ts:277 emits { schemaVersion, kind, data, principal } on every success, but cli-contract.md §2 — the document that declares itself the canonical envelope spec — shows a three-field example and a three-row table, and the string 'principal' appears nowhere in the file. Surfaced by opum-cli-e2e measuring the shipped 0.7.0 envelope against the spec while qualifying the pair.

acceptanceCriteria.text: cli-contract.md §2 documents principal: its type, its always-null-until-ratified meaning, and that consumers must not depend on it yet
The §2 JSON example matches what successEnvelope() actually emits
A check or test ties the documented envelope fields to the SuccessEnvelope type so this drift cannot recur silently

implementationNotes: AC1: docs/reference/cli-contract.md §2 field table now documents principal (type null, reserved-until-ratified, not part of the stable contract yet). AC2: §2 JSON example updated to include "principal": null, matching src/output.ts's successEnvelope() field-for-field (verified by a new bun test asserting Object.keys equality). AC3: test/output.test.ts adds two tests reading the real doc off disk -- one comparing the §2 JSON example's Object.keys() to successEnvelope()'s, one asserting every emitted field is named in §2's text -- both mutation-tested (reverting either the example or the table row independently fails its corresponding test; restoring passes). lore check exits 0. lint/typecheck clean.
finalSummary: docs/reference/cli-contract.md §2 (JSON example + field table) now documents the principal field that src/output.ts's successEnvelope() has emitted since it was added: type null, reserved for a future ratified reference, always null today, and explicitly not part of the stable contract yet. Also corrected §8's quick-reference row for consistency. test/output.test.ts gained two tests that read the real doc off disk: one asserts the §2 JSON example's Object.keys() equal successEnvelope()'s (catches an example that drops/gains a field), one asserts every field successEnvelope() emits is named in §2's own text (catches a field-table omission even if the example is fixed) -- both independently mutation-tested by reverting the doc back to three fields (example-only, then table-only) and confirming each corresponding test fails, then restoring. bun run lint, bun run typecheck, and bun test test/output.test.ts are all clean; lore check exits 0.
